startup.name: Probo
startup.one_liner: We help you get compliant while you focus on your business.
startup.description: Acts as a startup's compliance team: sets the right requirements, handles docs, risks, controls and evidence, runs the audit and keeps everything current. Team of 6 in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the batch that starts at the as_of date, so the acceptance step is reported only for completeness: the prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent), and conditional on being accepted the forecast below is what matters. Team of 6 is larger than typical; the product is a clear painful problem for founders but the space is crowded.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because compliance automation is crowded: Vanta, Drata and Secureframe have raised large rounds, several YC companies already sell similar AI compliance agents, and differentiation between them is thin. The managed service pitch of acting as the compliance team raises margin questions, though a team of six and a clearly painful problem for founders would help in the interview.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window of 19.3 months (2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17). Compliance automation is a land grab led by Vanta, Drata and Secureframe, each with large funding, and YC has many entrants (Oneleet, Agency, Hiro). Oneleet reached an A, but Agency and Hiro show no later round in the data, so a seed above $1M needs a sharp wedge such as full managed service for early stage founders and clear ARR.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Likely end is stall or acquisition under $100M by a larger GRC or security vendor: Central was acquired, Agency and Hiro stayed seed level or less, and leaders are far ahead. A bigger outcome needs the managed service wedge to scale into a distinct segment.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mapping controls, collecting evidence through integrations and managing auditors is a known problem; AI helps with document drafting. The hard parts are the many integrations and audit relationships, which a six person team can build slowly.

takeover_risk.rationale: Leaders already ship AI agents and low priced startup tiers and have distribution; a managed service wedge is harder for them to copy.

narrative.headline: Large market but dominated by funded leaders; seed odds near the compliance anchor trimmed for crowding.
narrative.general_summary: Probo is a managed compliance service for startups, with a team of six in San Francisco. The compliance tag cohort gives 0.71 for ever reaching seed and the broader B2B cohort 0.61. Over the 19.3 month window I give 0.50 for a round above $1M, and 0.10 for Series A given seed. Vanta and Drata dominate and many YC entrants chase the same buyer, though a managed service wedge differs from pure software. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast made as of 2025-04-07 using only the YC batch description in the input file, with market-only web searches.
Forecast window is 19.3 months, from 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17.

Seed means an outside financing round above about $1M that closes inside the window, not the standard YC deal of about $500K; the seed and Series A probabilities are window probabilities, not ever probabilities.

The odds do not rank this company against other companies in the batch: in the 2026 winners test, team size, claimed traction and a hot sector did not separate raisers from non raisers, so the seed number stays near the cohort anchor.
Cohort anchors come from older and 2022 to 2024 batches and are partly right censored; funding coverage in the data is incomplete (lower, known and upper ranges quoted).
